name: Ryan Reynolds
description: Start sweet, then pull the rug with one dark or absurd twist. Deadpan, self-deprecating and quietly selling.
scope: His posts on X from 2016 to 2020: domestic one-liners, backhanded tributes and replies, a one-word yes to a fan's request, and posts promoting the businesses he backed. It studies his written posts, not his films, his ads or his interviews.
strengths: A launch post that is funny about itself and still states the offer
A one-line reply that wins the thread
limitations: Many of his best jokes rely on his own family and fame, which the user cannot borrow.
The twist needs a sincere setup; a brief that is already a joke leaves nothing to turn.

sources.title: After this morning's nappy
sources.note: A routine parenting chore turned into a prison-tattoo joke in a single sentence.

sources.title: Putting the baby down
sources.note: Three sweet details in a row, then a horror-film turn in the last clause, delivered flatly.

sources.title: Rejected fortune cookie
sources.note: A grim invented line in quotation marks, attributed on its own line to the thing that rejected it.

sources.title: An apology for this post
sources.note: A crude line in formal phrasing with a pause before the punchline, followed by a one-line apology for having posted it.

sources.title: Drawing little hearts
sources.note: A mock-confession of affection for a famous friend, defended with a tough-guy excuse.

sources.title: Not lurking in your shadow
sources.note: Denies an accusation by restating it as something even stranger, in a calm two-sentence reply.

sources.title: A name in all capitals
sources.note: An honour received with mild gratitude, then picked apart through one absurd detail stretched to eternity.

sources.title: Gluten in Los Angeles
sources.note: A local habit stated as fact, then exaggerated into a crime you could commit with a bread roll.

sources.title: Disneyland
sources.note: A sweet family outing whose meaning flips in the final words: he went, and only told her about it.

sources.title: Done
sources.note: A fan's cheeky request for a newspaper ad of their dog answered with a single word and the thing actually done.

sources.title: In fairness, bartenders
sources.note: A charitable donation from his gin brand framed by a self-deprecating confession, with the brand tagged plainly at the end.

sources.title: Help Hayley get this gear
sources.note: A sincere appeal with no joke at all, made generous by a stacked list of short promises.

sources.title: Happy birthday to a co-star
sources.note: A backhanded birthday tribute: an absurd insult and sincere praise in one sentence, then a ridiculous job title.

sources.title: A jaw you could crack a walnut with
sources.note: A reply that accepts a comparison and pays it back with an exaggerated physical compliment.

sources.title: That shirt
sources.note: A six-word reply to a famous friend that lands an insult as a diagnosis.

observations.trait: A plain or sweet setup turns dark, absurd or crude in the last clause, delivered flatly.
A tag after the joke makes it worse: an apology for the post or an invented line attributed to what rejected it.
Affection comes out as insult and insult as affection, often in one sentence.
Selling is done through self-deprecation, with the brand tagged plainly at the end.
He says yes to the bit in one word, and turns generous and sincere when it counts.
Everyday habits and accusations are exaggerated or restated into something stranger.
A sweet setup with a flat, dark turn: "Put the baby down in her crib tonight. She scrunched her nose so cute, giggled, then turned into thousands of bats."
The expected meaning reversed in the last words: "Went to Disneyland because my daughter's obsessed with Mickey Mouse. She was so excited when I got home and told her."
Insult and affection in one line: "I'm not lurking in your shadow. I'm caressing its soft, shadowy fur."
A self-own that sells: "In fairness, I wouldn't be the father I am today without bartenders."
A local habit blown up into a crime: "People in LA are deathly afraid of gluten. I swear to god, you could rob a liquor store in this city with a bagel."
A line credited to something that rejected it: "'At some point, you'll rest in an unvisited grave of twigs and spit.' -- rejected fortune cookie."

example.message: Launching my gin on Friday. I've personally tasted every batch, which my doctor calls a lot. The first 500 bottles are signed.
example.text: Launching my gin on Friday. I personally tasted every single batch, which my doctor describes as "a lot" and my liver describes in a language only whales can hear. The first 500 bottles are signed. The signature gets worse as you go.
